questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: When approaching a dangerous area like an intersection, keep your hands ready on the clutch lever and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: Which is NOT something your lane position should do?

options.text: Help you see and be seen.
Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.

questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see and be seen. It should keep you out of blind spots, help you avoid hazards, and give you a way to escape if needed. It should not block your escape route.

questions.question: Which is a bad reason to use your horn?

options.text: A driver next to you is too close to the car ahead.
Someone is sitting in a parked car.
You want people to notice your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to notice your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others before you pass them. Use it when you see a car driver too close to the vehicle ahead, when someone is in a parked car, or when you pass a pedestrian or cyclist. Do not use it just to get attention.

questions.question: What formation should a group of riders use when entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation to keep the group together with good spacing. Use single-file formation when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This allows experienced riders at the back of the group to watch them.

questions.question: What should an effective face shield avoid?
questions.explanation: An effective face shield should be scratch-free, let you see to the sides, fit securely, and allow air to pass through. It should not be airtight, because that causes fogging and makes it hard to see.

questions.question: What should you do when it starts to rain while riding?

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil that makes it slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Also, slow down on wet roads.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes occur?

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles at speeds under 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: What do you NOT need to adjust when carrying a passenger?
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger changes how your motorcycle sits. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlight, and mirrors. You do not need to adjust the brake light position.

questions.question: What protects your eyes from wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: When applying the front brake, you should:

options.text: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
Use only two fingers to grab the brake.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.
Stomp hard on the brake lever.

questions.correctAnswerText: Squeeze the lever firmly and gradually increase pressure.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever with all four fingers. Apply pressure smoothly and gradually.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, which part of your lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closer to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to cut back in before it is safe.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should not:
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, slow down, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes smoothly. Never brake quickly.

questions.question: The effects of marijuana can last for:
questions.explanation: Smoked marijuana affects you within minutes and lasts 2 to 4 hours. Eaten marijuana takes over an hour to start working but can last more than 6 hours.

questions.question: When riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway, the best group formation is:
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation on straight roads. Switch to single-file when riding through curves, making turns, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Small vehicles can appear ______ and seem to be traveling ______ than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Small vehicles like motorcycles look farther away and slower than they really are. This makes it hard for other drivers to judge their actual distance and speed.

questions.question: The center of a lane often has an oily strip. This area is:

options.text: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
Usually safe, unless it is sunny outside.
Always safe, no matter the weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually safe, unless the road is wet.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars collects in a strip down the center of lanes. When dry, this area has good traction. When wet, avoid it. The strip is usually narrow, so you can ride beside it and still be in the center part of the lane.

questions.question: When you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, a rider should:

options.text: Perform one action, then the other.
Perform both actions at the same time and apply extra braking pressure.
Perform both actions at the same time, but mainly focus on swerving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Perform one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time. You need traction to swerve safely. Do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: When loading cargo on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Pack lighter items near the front.
Try to not place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Load heavy items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Placing weight behind the rear axle reduces your control.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Use your high beam (unless following or meeting another vehicle), use other vehicles' lights to help you see, and wear reflective clothing. Move around in your lane to see better, be seen, and maintain a safe distance cushion.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black letters or symbols. These signs tell you the traffic rules you must follow.

questions.question: Riders wearing helmets are ________ more likely to survive a crash than riders without helmets.
questions.explanation: A helmet makes you three times more likely to survive a head injury in a crash, at any speed.

questions.question: If your motorcycle has convex mirrors and you are unfamiliar with them, you should practice because:

options.text: Most people are not used to using mirrors.
They make objects look farther away than they really are.
They make objects look closer than they really are.
It is hard to remember to look at mirrors while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make objects look farther away than they really are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors give a wider view of the road behind you. But they make objects look farther away than they actually are. Practice using them so you get used to this difference.

questions.question: Studies show that most riders in crashes:

options.text: Do not brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
Brake the front tire too much and do not brake the rear tire enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.
questions.explanation: Most riders in crashes do not brake the front tire enough and brake the rear tire too much.

questions.question: A wobble or shaking of the front wheel and handlebars may be caused by:

options.text: Brakes that are not working properly.

questions.explanation: Most wobbles happen because of wrong tire pressure, improper loading, or unsuitable accessories.

questions.question: When you park a motorcycle next to a curb, it should be:

options.text: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
At a 45-degree angle with the front tire touching the curb.
Like a car, with the front and rear wheels the same distance from the curb.
At the left edge of the parking space so drivers can see it more easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a 90-degree angle with the rear wheel touching the curb.
questions.explanation: Park at a 90-degree angle to the curb with your rear wheel touching it.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, you should:

options.text: Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left portion of the lane.
Always ride in the right portion of the lane.
Change position based on different conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change position based on different conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position for all situations. Choose the position where drivers can see you best and where you have space around you.

questions.question: When it starts to rain, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is slippery when wet. Ride in the tire tracks left by cars instead. The left tire track is often the best choice.

questions.question: A rider without a helmet is ________ more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, a rider is five times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you from behind, you should:

options.text: Move to the center of the lane.
Move to the left portion of the lane.
Move to the right portion of the lane.
Not worry about your lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Staying too close to the passing vehicle increases crash risk.
